overview: The NEO-6M listens to satellite signals and reports position, altitude, speed, and precise time over a plain UART connection, streaming standardized NMEA sentences that a library (like TinyGPS++) parses into usable coordinates. The most important thing to know before using one: it needs a genuinely clear view of the sky — indoors, or even near tall buildings, it can take a very long time to get a fix or fail entirely — and a brand-new module doing a 'cold start' (no prior almanac data) can take 30 seconds to several minutes to find its first fix, even outdoors, though subsequent fixes are much faster thanks to a small backup battery that retains satellite data through power-off.
simpleSummary: A module that listens to satellites and reports your exact location.

specifications.timeToFirstFix: Cold start: ~30s-several minutes; warm/hot start (with battery-backed almanac): a few seconds

pinMap.name: VCC
pinMap.currentLimit: ~45 mA while acquiring, less once tracking

pinMap.name: TXD
pinMap.function: Serial transmit — continuously streams NMEA sentences whether or not a fix has been acquired.
pinMap.gotcha: Receiving NMEA data does NOT mean you have a valid position fix — check the fix-quality field in the sentence, don't assume any data means a valid location.

pinMap.name: RXD
pinMap.function: Serial receive, accepts configuration commands (e.g. changing output sentence rate).

pinMap.name: PPS
pinMap.function: Pulse-per-second output — a precisely-timed pulse once per second once a fix is acquired, useful for high-accuracy timing applications.
pinMap.gotcha: Not present on all breakout boards — only useful for projects needing GPS-disciplined timing, not plain positioning.

useCases.title: GPS-logging robot/drone
useCases.scenario: Record a path traveled or navigate to waypoint coordinates.

useCases.title: Vehicle tracker
useCases.scenario: Combine with a GSM module (SIM800L) to periodically report location remotely.

useCases.title: Precise clock synchronization
useCases.scenario: Use the PPS output for GPS-disciplined precise timekeeping.

oftenConfusedWith: Cellular-based location (much lower accuracy, no line-of-sky requirement)
oftenUpgradedTo: RTK-capable GPS modules for centimeter-level accuracy
